'''''Anacis verticillata''''' (synonym ''Coreopsis verticillata'') is a [[North America]]n [[species]] of [[Coreopsis|tickseed]] in the [[Asteraceae|sunflower family]]. It is found primarily in the east-central [[United States]], from [[Maryland]] south to [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]], with isolated populations as far west as [[Oklahoma]] and as far north as [[Québec]] and [[Ontario]].<ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Coreopsis%20verticillata.png Biota of North America Program 2014 county distribution map]</ref> The [[common names]] are '''whorled tickseed''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref><ref>{{PLANTS|id=COVE5|taxon=Coreopsis verticillata|accessdate=17 January 2016}}</ref> '''whorled coreopsis''', '''thread-leaved tickseed''', '''thread leaf coreopsis''', and '''pot-of-gold'''.

==Description==
''Anacis verticillata'' is an [[herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] that grows {{convert|2|-|3|ft|0|abbr=on}} tall and about {{convert|2|ft|0|abbr=on}} wide, although as it spreads laterally by [[rhizomes]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wildflower.org/plants/result.php?id_plant=cove5 |title=Coreopsis verticillata L. |access-date=2010-02-20|work=Wildflower Center at The University Of Texas At Austin }}</ref> this width can be exceeded. The [[Plant stem|stems]] are wiry.<ref name="Floridata">{{cite web|url=http://www.floridata.com/ref/C/core_ver.cfm |title=Coreopsis verticillata |access-date=2010-02-20 |last=Christman |first=Steve |publisher=Floridata }}</ref> The flower heads are up to {{convert|2|in|0|abbr=on}} across, and both the [[disc floret]]s and [[ray floret]]s are bright yellow. The flowers are produced abundantly in clusters from midsummer to fall.<ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=250066435 Flora of North America, ''Coreopsis verticillata'' Linnaeus, Sp. Pl. 2: 907. 1753. ]</ref>

==Habitat==
''Anacis verticillata'' can commonly be found in dry, thin woods and open [[pine barrens|pinelands]], preferring sites with full sun exposure. It can tolerate drought, poor soil, extreme heat, and neglect.<ref name="Floridata"/>

==Horticultural cultivation== 

Horticultural [[cultivar]]s of ''Anacis verticillata''  are not difficult to grow and hence make good starter plants for beginning gardeners in the U.S.<ref name="Perennial"/> They have a long flowering season and are relatively free from pests and diseases.<ref name="Perennial"/> They attract butterflies and are deer resistant.<ref name="Perennial">{{cite web |url=http://www.perennialresource.com/plants/general-perennial/177_coreopsis-verticillata-moonbeam.aspx |title=Coreopsis verticillata 'Moonbeam' |access-date=2010-02-20 |work=Perennial Resource |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110715064026/http://www.perennialresource.com/plants/general-perennial/177_coreopsis-verticillata-moonbeam.aspx |archive-date=2011-07-15 |url-status=dead }}</ref> They can be grown in hanging baskets and containers (where irrigation will be necessary), or as border plants.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.magnoliagardensnursery.com/productdescrip/Coreopsis_Moon.html |title=Coreopsis verticillata |access-date=2010-02-20 |work=Magnolia Gardens Nursery |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090528001258/http://www.magnoliagardensnursery.com/productdescrip/Coreopsis_Moon.html |archive-date=2009-05-28 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Carolyn Singer, in ''"Deer in My Garden",'' reports that ''A. verticillata'' is a good companion plant with other summer-blooming perennials requiring similar conditions.<ref>{{cite book | last = Singer | first = Carolyn | title = Deer in My Garden: Vol. 1: Perennials & Subshrubs | publisher = Emerald Book | year = 2006 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=QwCUO-KaZREC&q=Coreopsis+verticillata&pg=PA63 | isbn = 978-0-9774251-0-5 }}</ref> The following notable cultivars have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]]:
* 'Grandiflora' - taller than other cultivars, with slightly larger flowers<ref>{{cite web|url=http://apps.rhs.org.uk/plantselector/plant?plantid=528 |title=RHS Plant Selector Coreopsis verticillata 'Grandiflora' AGM / RHS Gardening |publisher=Apps.rhs.org.uk |access-date=2013-06-06}}</ref>
* 'Moonbeam' - pale, sulphur-yellow flowers, slightly shorter growth, chosen as the 1992 Perennial Plant of the Year by the Perennial Plant Association.<ref name="Floridata"/> When this cultivar was first introduced to the market, demand outstripped supply in some localities, such was its popularity.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://gardening.about.com/od/plantprofile1/ig/Coreopsis--Tickseed-/Coreopsis--Moonbeam-.htm |title=Coreopsis verticillata 'Moonbeam' |access-date=2010-02-20 |last=Iannotti |first=Marie |work=About.com |archive-date=2013-01-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130117101735/http://gardening.about.com/od/plantprofile1/ig/Coreopsis--Tickseed-/Coreopsis--Moonbeam-.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://apps.rhs.org.uk/plantselector/plant?plantid=4419 |title=RHS Plant Selector Coreopsis verticillata 'Moonbeam' / RHS Gardening |publisher=Apps.rhs.org.uk |access-date=2013-06-06}}</ref>
* 'Zagreb' - shorter than most ''Anacis'' or ''Coreopsis'' species, blooms with bright yellow flowers<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.northcreeknurseries.com/index.cfm/fuseaction/plants.plantDetail/plant_id/56/index.htm |title=Coreopsis verticillata ''Zagreb'' |access-date=2010-02-20 |work=North Creek Nurseries }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://apps.rhs.org.uk/plantselector/plant?plantid=529 |title=RHS Plant Selector Coreopsis verticillata 'Zagreb' AGM / RHS Gardening |publisher=Apps.rhs.org.uk |access-date=2013-06-06}}</ref>
